o1.biggest_strength: It spots the real win: bring back the paused 1-month pause for the no-time segment, and makes that the sprint-critical path with clear copy and economics.
o1.biggest_mistake: The £29,160 discount-saving line is worded as monthly when it appears to be the 3-month cohort discount cost, and the 12-month revenue projection needs clearer working.

o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the unsupported switcher discount, use billing variables instead of assumed prices, and tighten the revenue maths around discounts and annual-plan value.

reason: Output 1 is the one I would hand to product: it makes the pause the main build priority, respects the one-screen rule, gives warmer copy, and is more honest about where the forecast depends on untested assumptions. Output 2 is good, but the unsupported 50% switcher discount and customer-facing price assumption make it riskier.
